summary.en: Vocative, locative and instrumental, prepositions with u/na, pronouns in every case, and adjective agreement.
summary.bs: Vokativ, lokativ i instrumental, prijedlozi u/na, zamjenice u svim padežima i slaganje pridjeva.

en.one: The vokativ is the case for calling or addressing someone directly. It has no question; think 'hej!' (hey!).
en.explain: Masculine: often -e or -u: Amir → Amire!, prijatelj → prijatelju!, gospodin → gospodine! Feminine in -a: -o, but many names stay the same: žena → ženo!, Amra → Amra! (or Amro!), mama → mama! Neuter: same as nominative. Commas separate it from the sentence.
en.example: 'Dobar dan, gospodine Hadžiću!' 'Dragi prijatelju, hvala ti.' 'Mama, gdje si?'
en.why: Greetings, emails and letters all start with a vocative, and using it correctly sounds polite and native.
en.mixup: In emails write 'Poštovani gospodine Kovačiću' (Dear Mr Kovačić), not 'Poštovani gospodin Kovačić'.

en.one: The lokativ shows location or topic, and it is ALWAYS used after a preposition. Questions: o kome? o čemu? (gdje?)
en.explain: Endings are the same as the dative in the singular: masc./neut. -u (u gradu, na moru), fem. -i (u kući, o ženi). Plural: -ima/-ama (u gradovima, u kućama). Prepositions: u (in), na (on / at), o (about), po (around / according to), pri (at / during).
en.example: 'Živim u Sarajevu.' 'Knjiga je na stolu.' 'Pričamo o poslu.' 'Šetam po gradu.'
en.why: Every time you say where you are or what you talk about, you need the locative.
en.mixup: 'u' and 'na' + locative = where something IS. For where something GOES, use the accusative: u grad, na more (next cards).

en.one: The instrumental shows company (with whom?) or the tool or way you do something (with what? by what?). Questions: s kim? čim?
en.explain: Endings: masc./neut. -om/-em (autom, nožem, prijateljem), fem. -om (ženom, olovkom). Plural: -ima/-ama. With 'with' meaning company, use s/sa: 'sa sestrom'. For a tool or transport, use NO preposition: 'pišem olovkom' (I write with a pen), 'putujem vozom (vlakom)' (I travel by train).
en.example: 'Idem u kino s prijateljima.' 'Plaćam karticom.' 'Dolazim autobusom.'
en.why: Transport, payments and company all use the instrumental, so it's essential for daily life.
en.mixup: Don't add 's' for tools: 'Jedem viljuškom (vilicom)' (I eat with a fork), not 's viljuškom'. 's' is only for people and things that come along.

en.one: 'u' and 'na' can take two cases, and the question decides: gdje? (where?) → locative; kuda? / kamo? (where to?) → accusative.
en.explain: Location (gdje?): 'Ja sam u gradu.' 'Knjiga je na stolu.' Movement (kuda/kamo?): 'Idem u grad.' 'Stavljam knjigu na sto (stol).' 'u' is for inside spaces and cities; 'na' for surfaces, open places, events and some fixed places: na poslu, na fakultetu, na moru, na koncertu.
en.example: 'Idem na posao' (A) → 'Ja sam na poslu' (L). 'Idem u Zagreb' (A) → 'Živim u Zagrebu' (L).
en.why: This pair is in nearly every sentence about places, and German uses exactly the same logic (Wohin? / Wo?).
en.mixup: Learn whether a place takes 'u' or 'na' together with the word: u školu, but na fakultet; u banku, but na poštu.

en.one: Personal pronouns change with every case and most have a long (stressed) and a short (unstressed) form.
en.explain: ja: mene/me (G, A), meni/mi (D), mnom (I). ti: tebe/te, tebi/ti, tobom. on: njega/ga, njemu/mu, njim. ona: nje/je (G), njoj/joj (D), nju/je (A), njom. mi: nas, nama, nama. vi: vas, vama. oni: njih/ih, njima/im. Short forms are normal; long forms are for emphasis or after prepositions: 'Voli me' vs 'Voli MENE, ne tebe'; 'za mene', 'sa mnom'.
en.example: 'Daj mi to.' 'Vidim ga svaki dan.' 'Ideš li sa mnom?' 'Ovo je za tebe.'
en.why: Short pronouns are among the most frequent words. Without them your sentences sound heavy and over-stressed.
en.mixup: After a preposition always use the long form: 'za tebe', not 'za te' (except in a few fixed phrases).

en.one: Adjectives agree with their noun in gender, number and case. The adjective ending often looks like the noun's ending.
en.explain: Nominative: nov grad, nova kuća, novo selo, novi gradovi, nove kuće, nova sela. Accusative: vidim novi grad / novu kuću / novo selo. Genitive: novog(a) grada, nove kuće. Dative/locative: novom gradu, novoj kući. Instrumental: novim gradom, novom kućom. Short and long forms exist for masculine (nov / novi); the long form means 'the': 'novi grad' = the new town.
en.example: 'Živim u velikom gradu, u maloj kući s lijepim vrtom.'
en.why: Agreement shows you which words belong together, even when word order is free.
en.mixup: Croatian writes the masculine genitive often as -oga/-ega (novoga), Bosnian mostly -og (novog). Both are correct.
